newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: EBRD to help Slovenia build private pension scheme.
newsitem.headline: EBRD to help Slovenia build private pension scheme.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Thursday setting up a private pension scheme would be one of the main areas of its involvement in Slovenia for the next four to five years.

"Slovenia has a big burden of public pensions which take up 13 percent of national income. That is much higher than the OECD average of nine to 10 percent," EBRD chief economist Nicholas Stern told a news conference in Ljubljana.
"EBRD's role is to help build saving institutions....to help private pension institutions grow," Stern added.
At present some 25 percent of each gross salary goes into a public pension fund -- almost double the amount in 1986.
In 1994, Slovenia had 0.9 working persons for each retired or incapacitated, down from 1.7 in 1990 and 2.5 in 1985.
The EBRD would also participate in commercialising Slovenia's infrastructure, notably telecommunications, transport and the electrical power supply.
"Commercialisation of infrastructure is a part of the transition process and means focusing on costs, demand and consumers," Stern said.
Stern said the EBRD has invested more in Slovenia than in any other transition economy.

So far EBRD investment in Slovenia has totalled over 320 million Ecu ($410.6 million), equivalent to some 160 Ecu per capita. Stern said he expects a further 40 to 50 million Ecu to be invested in 1997, but gave no further details. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386 61 1263 644 ($1=.7794 Ecu)
